question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3. **
solution:
The correct answer is: '**is**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject in the sentence is "**the goodness**," which is a **singular noun**.
 
• In English, when the **subject is singular**, the **verb **should also be in the **singular **form.
 
• Therefore, the correct form is "**is**."
 
• The word "**is**" serves as the linking verb that connects the subject ("**the goodness**") with the complement ("**a common point worth mentioning**").

Thus, **option 3** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• "**Are**" is the plural form of the verb, and it doesn't agree with the singular subject "the goodness." The subject-verb agreement is not maintained.
 
• "**Am**" is the first-person singular form of the verb, used with the pronoun "I."
 
• "**On**" is a preposition, and it does not serve as the appropriate verb to connect the subject and complement in this sentence.
